text:
Kirill Kaprizov has 45 points in 25 games, and lately he has turned into a passer. His point streak reached 14 games in Saturday's shootout loss in Vancouver, and in that stretch he has 21 assists to 7 goals. Heather Rule of NHL.com counted 12 assists in his last five games alone. The Wild are 11-0-3 in their last 14, and Quinn Hughes has been running a matching streak beside him on the back end.

How much of this is real? Most of it. He shoots plenty and gets to good ice, 14.7 expected goals on his own shots. But 18 goals means he is shooting 24% against 17% last season, and the Wild have scored 14.5 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. That kind of luck fades, even for a former Calder winner.

So the number to watch is 5.02 points per 60 minutes. Our range for his true rate tops out near 3.9, still elite. Even with a cooldown built in, we project him for about 117 points.
headline: Kaprizov is driving the hottest team in hockey
